stem.text: The function \( f \) is defined by the power series \[ f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x + 2)^{n}}{3^{n}\sqrt{n}} \] for all real \( x \) for which the series converges.

parts.prompt: Use the ratio test to find the values of \( x \) for which the series for \( f(x) \) converges absolutely. Give your answer as an open interval.

worked_solution.text: Form the ratio of consecutive terms in absolute value.
Take the limit as n grows.
Set the limit less than 1 and solve.

points.criterion: Writes the ratio of the (n+1)st term to the nth term, (x + 2)^(n+1)/(3^(n+1) sqrt(n+1)) divided by (x + 2)^n/(3^n sqrt(n)), or a simplified form such as (|x + 2|/3) sqrt(n/(n+1)), with or without absolute values.
Evaluates the limit of the ratio as |x + 2|/3 with correct limit notation; any error in simplifying or evaluating the limit loses this point.
Resolves |x + 2|/3 < 1 to the two-sided inequality -5 < x < 1 or the interval (-5, 1); |x + 2| < 3 left unresolved does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Determine whether the series for \( f(x) \) converges at each endpoint of the interval from part (a), and state the interval of convergence of the series. Justify your answers.

worked_solution.text: At x = 1 the series is a p-series with p = 1/2.
Since p = 1/2 is at most 1, this series diverges.
Its terms 1/sqrt(n) decrease to 0, so it converges by the alternating series test.

points.criterion: Substitutes both x = 1 and x = -5 and writes the two resulting numerical series, the sum of 1/sqrt(n) and the sum of (-1)^n/sqrt(n).

Concludes that the series at x = 1 diverges as a p-series with p = 1/2 (or by comparison with the harmonic series) and that the series at x = -5 converges by the alternating series test, and states the interval of convergence -5 <= x < 1 or [-5, 1).

parts.prompt: Let \( h \) be the function defined by \[ h(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x + 2)^{n+1}}{(n + 1)\,3^{n}\sqrt{n}} \] for all real \( x \) for which the series converges. Find the interval of convergence of the series for \( h(x) \). Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: Ratio of consecutive terms in absolute value.
Its limit, which is less than 1 exactly when -5 < x < 1.
At x = 1 the terms are positive and bounded by a convergent p-series with p = 3/2.
At x = -5 the absolute values of the terms are the same, so the series converges absolutely.

points.criterion: Writes the ratio of consecutive terms of the series for h, (x + 2)^(n+2)/((n + 2)3^(n+1) sqrt(n+1)) divided by (x + 2)^(n+1)/((n + 1)3^n sqrt(n)), or a simplified form, with or without absolute values.
Evaluates the limit of that ratio as |x + 2|/3 with correct limit notation and concludes the series converges for -5 < x < 1; an error in the limit loses this point.
Substitutes both x = 1 and x = -5 into the series for h and writes the two resulting series, the sum of 3/((n + 1)sqrt(n)) and the sum of 3(-1)^(n+1)/((n + 1)sqrt(n)).

Concludes both endpoint series converge, at x = 1 by comparison or limit comparison with the convergent p-series of 1/n^(3/2), and at x = -5 by absolute convergence through the same comparison or by the alternating series test, and states the interval of convergence -5 <= x <= 1 or [-5, 1].
